profile.headline: Senior Robotics Software Engineer @ DEKA Research & Development | Autonomous Vehicles | Localization | SLAM | Computer Vision | Embedded Software | University of Michigan | IIT Bombay
profile.summary: Senior Robotics Software Engineer with 5+ years of experience designing and deploying robust localization and mapping systems for real-world autonomous robots. Expertise in LiDAR–IMU SLAM, sensor fusion, and performance-critical C++ systems, with proven technical leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and on-robot deployment.

positions.title: Senior Robotics Software Engineer - Localization & Mapping
Localization Engineer
positions.description: Implementing Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter algorithm (Sensor Fusion) in Python for precise vehicle geopositioning using GNSS and IMU sensors, aiming to develop a fully automated parking payment and guidance system

positions.title: ADAS System Intern
positions.description:
Project: Development of ADAS L-2 features (AEB, FCW, ACC, LKA) using a vehicle simulation platform
• Developing sensor fusion algorithms and vehicle control algorithms using sensor data from RADAR, Cameras, etc
• Developed AEB brake control logic using Simulink-Stateflow and implemented autonomous multi-modal (AMM) algorithm to predict the target vehicle’s trajectory and estimate the time-to-collision (TTC)
• Integrating perception, tracking, planning and control subsystems in MATLAB/Simulink for MIL & SIL testing

positions.title: Mechatronic System Design
positions.description:
• Modeled and implemented physical mechatronic systems integrated with sensors, actuators and control systems to achieve various system-level performance objectives such as command tracking, stability, noise rejection, etc.
• Developed real-time feedback control (PID, lead-lag, LQR) for systems such as DC motor, inverted pendulum, etc.
• Deployed real-time controls on hardware through sensors and actuators by using LabVIEW and myRIO

positions.title: Summer Research Intern, HaptiX Lab
positions.description:
Project Title: Haptic Shared Control in Semi-Autonomous Driving
Guide: Professor Brent Gillespie, Department of Mechanical Engineering
• Collaborated with Toyota Research Institute to improve human takeover transition in semi-autonomous driving
• Developed coupled and decoupled control algorithms using pure pursuit controller in MATLAB/Simulink
• Designed virtual driving scenarios in CarSim (integrated with Simulink) with different weather and traffic conditions
• Developed test procedures to analyze control algorithms on factors such as comfort level and collision avoidance

positions.title: Student Mechanical Design Engineer -  Multidisciplinary Design Program
positions.description:
Project Title: Laminate Breakaway Modeling and Simulation of Airbag Deployment
• Collaborated with multidisciplinary team of 6 student peers to investigate an anomaly in airbag deployment
• Characterized material properties of laminate layers and whole composite using tensile tests and linear impact tests
• Led simulation subteam to successfully design a multiphysics simulation model using HyperWorks and ABAQUS

projects.title: Mechatronic's Lab
projects.description:
Graduate Course:  Mechatronic System Design
Guide: Professor Shorya Awtar, Department of Mechanical Engineering
Modeled and implemented physical hardware, and developed control strategies (PID, lead-lag, LQR) for:
- Magnetic Levitation System
- DC-Servo Motor System
- Inverted Pendulum System
- Stepper Motor System

projects.title: Posable Inflatable Tensegrity Structures
projects.description:
Graduate Research Assistant:  Smart Materials and Structures Lab
Guide: Professor Diann Brei, Department of Mechanical Engineering
- Conceptualized the posability enhancement of inflatable structures by developing the internal tensegrity kinematics
- Conducted characteristic experiments for tensegrity interaction and fabricated prototypes to achieve posability
